newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian Merukh says in Busang talks with Bre-X.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian Merukh says in Busang talks with Bre-X.

text.p: Indonesian businessman Jusuf Merukh said on Monday he had put off a $1.9 billion lawsuit against Bre-X Minerals Ltd because the Canadian mining company had begun discussions over the Busang gold find. "I am delaying the legal action because Bre-X has been in touch with my lawyers," he told Reuters.
Merukh, who claims to own 40 percent of the Busang find, estimated by Bre-X to contain at least 47 million ounces of gold, declined to give further details.
Bre-X and Merukh have been locked in an ownership dispute that led to the Indonesian government to delay issuing a contract of work (COW) until they resolved the quarrel.
Merukh had given Bre-X until December 4 to commence meaningful negotiations or face legal action.

The government has since advised Bre-X to partner Barrick Gold Corp to develop Busang, with Bre-X taking a 25- percent stake and Barrick 75 percent. It has given both parties until December 4 to strike a deal.
The government has also indicated that it wanted a 10-percent stake to be allocated by Bre-X and Barrick.
Warren Beckwith, president of Golden Valley Mines NL of Australia, which has a technical assistance and finance deal with Merukh, confirmed on Monday that Merukh's legal action has been delayed.
"We will hold on (to the lawsuit) since we are having meaningful discussions," he added.
Beckwith said that the amount of revenue Golden Valley will get from its deal with Merukh will depend on "how things will go when the mine goes into operation".
"The revenue will partly be based on royalties. There are figures in the agreement (with Merukh)," he added.
Beckwith said he was confident that Golden Valley and Merukh would get their share of Busang as "I'm sure the government will take measures to make sure the rights of all parties are protected".

Meanwhile, Mines Department secretary-general Umar Said held talks with a delegation from the Indonesia Mining Association and told them that 68 COWs were awaiting final approval from President Suharto.
"He told us that the application by Bre-X, however, was not among them," one source told Reuters.
"If both Bre-X and Barrick can work out a deal by the December 4 deadline, the application of Bre-X for a contract of work will be approved with the others," the source said.
The contract will allow Bre-X to commence exploration of the richest parts of the Busang find in East Kalimantan.
